frontend.prompt:
Scope: apply only to the two specific error instances named in the requirement (the same two instances the backend will change). Do not change other error.message usages.

Implementation steps:
1) Code changes
   - Replace all front-end code that reads error.message for the two specified error responses to read error.detail instead, using the same access path under the error object (i.e., response.error.detail).
   - Keep all decision logic that depends on response.error.code exactly as-is; do not switch to matching natural-language content. Use code values exclusively for branching/behavior.
   - Do not read or expect a top-level detail field. Always access detail via response.error.detail.

2) UI / display
   - For user-visible text, display response.error.detail where the old workflow displayed response.error.message.
   - Ensure any logs or debug output that previously logged response.error.message now logs response.error.detail.

3) Tests
   - Update unit and integration tests that asserted on error.message to assert on error.detail instead.
   - Add tests that verify the following acceptance conditions for the two changed cases:
     • The response has an error object (response.error exists).
     • response.error.detail exists and contains the natural-language text (string).
     • response.error.message is absent (deleted).
     • response.request_id remains present and unchanged.
     • response.error.code remains present and is used for decision logic (tests must assert behavior still derives from code, not detail text).
     • There is no top-level response.detail.

4) Deployment coordination
   - Coordinate deployment with backend so front-end and backend changes roll out together (same release window). Front-end will rely on the backend serving error.detail instead of error.message after the backend change.

Acceptance tests (to run after backend change is deployed or in a coordinated test environment):
   - For each of the two changed error responses, call the API and assert:
     • response.error is present.
     • response.error.detail is present and is the expected natural-language string for the scenario.
     • response.error.message is not present.
     • response.request_id is present.
     • front-end behavior (navigation/UI state) is driven by response.error.code and matches the expected behavior for that code.

Notes / constraints:
   - Do not implement any logic that treats error.detail as a replacement for code-based decisions.
   - Do not modify other API error.message locations beyond the two specified cases.

backend.prompt:
Scope: change only the two specific error.message fields referenced in the requirement. Do not alter other error.message occurrences or other error-response formats.

Implementation steps:
1) Code changes
   - In the two specified error-generation locations, rename the field error.message to error.detail. The string content currently assigned to error.message must be copied to error.detail.
   - Remove the old error.message property from those responses so it no longer appears in the JSON output.
   - Preserve response.request_id exactly as it is today (no renaming or relocation).
   - Ensure the error object remains nested under the response's error property (do not create or populate a top-level detail field).
   - Do not change error.code values or types; maintain existing code values used by clients for logic.

2) API schema & docs
   - Update any OpenAPI/JSON Schema / API documentation entries corresponding to the two changed responses: replace error.message with error.detail in those response schemas.
   - If schema generation is automated from models, update the model definitions used for those two error responses so generated schemas reflect error.detail (and no error.message).

3) Tests
   - Update unit tests and server-side tests that asserted on error.message to assert on error.detail instead.
   - Add/modify integration tests for each of the two changed responses that assert all of the following acceptance conditions:
     • The HTTP response body contains an error object (response.error exists).
     • response.error.detail exists and contains the expected human-readable string for that error case.
     • response.error.message does not appear anywhere in the response body.
     • response.request_id remains present and unchanged.
     • response.error.code remains present and unchanged.
     • There is no top-level response.detail field.

4) Backward-compatibility and rollout
   - This change removes error.message for the two specified responses. Coordinate with the front-end team to deploy their corresponding changes at the same release window so clients do not experience breakage.
   - Do not introduce in-band fallback fields or alternate top-level fields unless explicitly agreed by both teams; follow the instruction to remove message and add detail inside error.

5) Logging / telemetry
   - If server logs or telemetry currently reference error.message for these two cases, update logging to reference error.detail to keep logs consistent. Ensure request_id continues to be logged with the error for traceability.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before marking done):
   - For each of the two changed error responses, automated tests verify: response.error exists; response.error.detail exists with expected text; response.error.message is absent; response.request_id is present; response.error.code unchanged; no top-level detail present.

Notes / constraints:
   - Only modify the two specific error occurrences named in the requirement. Do not change other API error structures.
   - Do not move detail to top-level or otherwise change the nesting of the error object.
   - Do not rely on or implement any contract changes not explicitly stated in the requirement.
